13: /// ## What it does
14: /// Checks for unnecessary dictionary unpacking operators (`**`).
15: ///
16: /// ## Why is this bad?
17: /// Unpacking a dictionary into another dictionary is redundant. The unpacking
18: /// operator can be removed, making the code more readable.
19: ///
20: /// ## Example
21: /// ```python
22: /// foo = {"A": 1, "B": 2}
23: /// bar = {**foo, **{"C": 3}}
24: /// ```
25: ///
26: /// Use instead:
27: /// ```python
28: /// foo = {"A": 1, "B": 2}
29: /// bar = {**foo, "C": 3}
30: /// ```
31: ///
32: /// ## References
33: /// - [Python documentation: Dictionary displays](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/expressions.html#dictionary-displays)
34: #[derive(ViolationMetadata)]
35: pub(crate) struct UnnecessarySpread;
36: 
37: impl Violation for UnnecessarySpread {
38:     const FIX_AVAILABILITY: FixAvailability = FixAvailability::Sometimes;
39: 
40:     #[derive_message_formats]
41:     fn message(&self) -> String {
42:         "Unnecessary spread `**`".to_string()
43:     }
44: 
45:     fn fix_title(&self) -> Option<String> {
46:         Some("Remove unnecessary dict".to_string())
47:     }
48: }

50: /// PIE800
51: pub(crate) fn unnecessary_spread(checker: &mut Checker, dict: &ast::ExprDict) {
52:     // The first "end" is the start of the dictionary, immediately following the open bracket.
53:     let mut prev_end = dict.start() + TextSize::from(1);
54:     for ast::DictItem { key, value } in dict {
55:         if key.is_none() {
56:             // We only care about when the key is None which indicates a spread `**`
57:             // inside a dict.
58:             if let Expr::Dict(inner) = value {
59:                 let mut diagnostic = Diagnostic::new(UnnecessarySpread, value.range());
60:                 if let Some(fix) = unnecessary_spread_fix(inner, prev_end, checker.locator()) {
61:                     diagnostic.set_fix(fix);
62:                 }
63:                 checker.diagnostics.push(diagnostic);
64:             }
65:         }
66:         prev_end = value.end();
67:     }
68: }
